correctness.rationale: The graph has diameter two and exactly computed common-neighbor intervals. For max(m,n)>=4 a same-row or same-column pair fills the graph in finitely many rigorously specified steps, while partial permutation matrices are convex. The 3x3 cross lemma identifies exactly six maximal proper convex sets, and 63-term inclusion-exclusion gives every coefficient. Separate breadth-first-search verification exhausts 107008 vertex subsets over five complete small graphs; no finite experiment is substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural all-sizes hull polynomial, not just a scalar optimum, in a two-parameter family of dense, diameter-two graphs. An exact structural dichotomy (generic partial permutations versus exceptional 3x3 complements of full permutations) produces a closed polynomial for all dimensions, a sharp finite obstruction, and exact extremal set counts. These distinguish iterative hull closure from one-step geodetic coverage.
